# Vibe Coding

> An MIT-licensed Windows skill for delegating VS Code environment setup to an AI agent. Made by AI찬우쌤 (Hong Chanwoo), creator of 클래스똑딱 / classddok.com.

Current release: v2.8.2. This is environment automation, not a model, hosted coding service, or replacement for Codex.

## Start here
- [Project and introduction video](https://arthong1.github.io/vsstudiovibecoding/): Korean landing page, 35-second video, installation request, creator links.
- [Repository](https://github.com/ARTHONG1/vsstudiovibecoding): Source code and issue tracker.
- [Skill instructions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ARTHONG1/vsstudiovibecoding/v2.8.2/vibe-coding/SKILL.md): Read before setup; preserve existing projects and settings.
- [Release](https://github.com/ARTHONG1/vsstudiovibecoding/releases/tag/v2.8.2): Windows skill ZIP.
- [Verification and limitations](https://github.com/ARTHONG1/vsstudiovibecoding/blob/main/TESTING.md): Automated checks are distinct from real phone rendering.

- [English quick start](https://github.com/ARTHONG1/vsstudiovibecoding/blob/main/README.en.md): Installation, capabilities and boundaries.
- [Media and descriptions](https://github.com/ARTHONG1/vsstudiovibecoding/blob/main/SHARING.md): Copy-ready Korean and English descriptions.

## What the agent prepares
Inspect the actual project, identify its startup command and verified preview URL, install an isolated VS Code environment, prepare Preview / Code / Codex layout and a desktop shortcut. Full setup includes Playwright CLI and its skill, Context7 MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, and contextual project instructions. Login, trust prompts, external-service access, and human approvals remain separate.

Mobile work uses Microsoft's official tunnel. The PC stays online. Private devtunnels previews open in a separate browser tab for authentication; return to vscode.dev for terminal work. The port-forwarding CLI protocol is version-dependent. Phone rendering must be tested; never claim universal or error-free support.
